newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Kvaerner profits down, divy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Kvaerner profits down, divy unchanged.

text.p: Norway's Kvaerner ASA on Tuesday booked 1996 operating profits at 1.03 billion crowns ($154.8 million), down 48 percent from a year ago, and said it did not foresee any improvement until the second half of 1997.
The London-based engineering and construction group proposed to keep its dividend unchanged at 6.50 crowns/0.60p per share.
Kvaerner, which acquired Britain's Trafalgar House in April, said turnover almost doubled reaching 58.56 billion crowns, against 30.19 billion crowns a year earlier.
But operating expenses rose to 56.20 billion crowns from 27.33 billion crowns.
Pre-tax profits amounted to 750 million crowns versus 2.44 billion crowns. The figures included a profit of 810 million crowns from the sale of ships and other assets.
"The 1996 results are most unsatisfactory," Erik Tonseth, president and chief executive, said in a statement.

"Cost reductions and restructuring will continue in 1997, but with continuing pressure on margins and short-term overcapacity in some businesses, it is unlikely that profits will improve significantly until the second half of 1997."

The figures were below market expectations, mainly due to a reversal of a 120 million crown gain booked in the third quarter because of an adjustment in the opening balance from the acquisition of Trafalgar House.

Despite the decline, analysts said the results on a divisional level were encouraging and at 1200 GMT Kvaerner's A share was up eight crowns at 341 crowns, while the B had advanced seven crowns to 311 crowns.
"The underlying operating profit in Kvaerner is showing signs of strengthening," said one analyst.

"An improving trend has materialised in the core businesses in the fourth quarter. Kvaerner usually has to defend its figures but now it appears to be dealing more pro-actively with the problem areas."

Pre-tax profits in shipbuilding amounted to 1.04 billion crowns over the 12-month period, against 1.52 billion crowns. Total order intake was 7.9 billion crowns, bringing the order backlog to 14.6 billion crowns.
Kvaerner said eight months of earnings from the ex-Trafalgar process division led to profits before tax of 145 million crowns, while metals exceeded expectations at 100 million crowns for the period.

Construction, another Trafalgar unit, posted a result before tax of 32 million crowns. "The underlying trading performance of the business area (construction) in the quarter to 31 December 1996 continued to improve," Kvaerner's statement said.
It said the oil and gas sector had concluded "a very disappointing year" with a pre-tax loss of 33 million crowns versus a 1995 profit of 276 million crowns.

Pulp and paper moved further into the red, running a loss for the year of 266 million crowns, including a 167 million crown gain from the sale of shares in Finnish Tampella Corp. In 1995 pulp and paper had a pre-tax loss of 178 million crowns.

"The Pulp & Paper activities have been restructured into product and industry streams and cost reduction initiatives are being implemented to achieve annual savings of some 350 million crowns," the company said.

Under other business, Kvaerner said a steep downturn in results in the fourth quarter reflected the significance of problems at Kvaerner Energy, where provisions had been made to cut annual costs by 350 million crowns.
Other activities showed a pre-tax loss of 255 million crowns compared with a profit of 813 million crowns a year ago.

The Cunard cruise liner unit delivered a weak result in the fourth quarter, while the plastics machinery business, U.S. housebuilding and Trafalgar House property all made profits in line with expectations.
($ = 6.654 Norwegian Crowns)
